statusText: WATCH - Tail 20 of 100 in the watch band, below the block threshold; Stress 75 high; Confidence 88 high.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains WATCH. Tail eases a further point to 20 because the evidence continues to show mean reversion being granted rather than denied: the 28,913.49 session low has now stood for about three and a half hours, the index sits roughly 49 points above it, and VIX has decayed to 17.46 from an 18.03 session high even while the index trades near the lower end of its range. That is non-confirmation rather than aligned stress. The long end has also steadied after the 20-year auction, with the 10-year at 5.01% and the 2-year essentially unchanged at 4.67%. The published danger window stays at the 19:00Z-20:00Z power hour, the last evidence-based checkpoint before the cash close. Stress stays high at 75 on WTI near $105.77, Brent near $108.78 and a 10-year at its highest since 2007.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its session low for a third hour while VIX decays off its high and the long end steadies after the 20-year auction, easing Tail to 20 in the watch band with crude near $106 and the FOMC decision a day away
body:
The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades near 28,962.43, down 0.57% against a 29,127.16 previous close, inside a session range of 28,913.49 to 29,142.80 that spans about 0.79%. The decisive observation this hour is durability: the session low set in the mid-session has now survived roughly three and a half hours and one scheduled supply checkpoint, the 17:00Z 20-year auction that stopped at 5.420%. The index has since ticked up rather than down, sitting about 49 points above the low and about 180 points below the high, while NQ futures near 29,268.25 are down 0.62% with their own 29,218.00 low likewise intact. Extensions continue to be followed by usable retracements and no new session low has printed. Mean reversion is being granted, which is the specific condition that keeps Tail inside the watch band and supports a second consecutive one-point reduction.

Cross-asset evidence is notably unaligned, which is a further argument against a pathological path. VIX at 17.46 is up 2.11% on the day but is trading below its 18.03 session high and below the level recorded an hour ago, declining while the index sits near its lows. The long end has steadied after the auction: the 10-year is at 5.01%, its highest since 2007 but a touch below the 5.02% print earlier in the session, the 20-year is at 5.41% and the 2-year is essentially unchanged at 4.67%, so the curve is not repricing in one direction. Index internals conflict as well. Semiconductors are broadly higher, with Qualcomm up 4.51%, AMD up 1.80% and Nvidia up 0.23%, while the megacap complex is mostly lower, with Amazon down 1.88%, Broadcom down 1.89% and Alphabet down 1.79%. Sector breadth is moderately negative rather than severe, technology down 0.41% against consumer cyclical down 1.30%. Conflicting internals of this kind raise Stress and reduce directional conviction; they do not establish the persistent one-way structure that Tail measures.

The macro backdrop is why Stress stays high at 75. Crude has extended sharply, with WTI up about 4.3% to $105.77 and Brent up about 2.9% to $108.78, after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline following attacks and Libya suspended output at two fields. Reporting puts the pipeline repair at three to five weeks, so this is an open supply disruption rather than a resolved one, and crude has risen roughly 20% this month. The September Empire State manufacturing index, released at 12:30Z, fell thirteen points to 7.6 against a 14.75 consensus while its prices-paid component rose to 63.1, a combination that reinforces the inflation channel behind the move in yields. Looking forward, the calendar is dense: U.S. retail sales for August is scheduled for 12:30Z Wednesday and the FOMC decision, projections and press conference follow at 18:00Z and 18:30Z, with markets currently pricing a high probability of a 25 basis point increase. None of those outcomes is known, and none is assumed here. Consistent with the calibration used in this series, scheduled event importance and forecast dispersion are carried in Stress and Confidence, while Tail is raised materially only once an observed price path denies retracement. The FOMC instant falls just beyond this 24-hour horizon.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Tail ranged from 14 to 25 and spent a single hour in the block band, at the 08:00Z European-morning slot. The U.S. evening and Asian stretch was the calmest of the cycle, with Tail between 14 and 16 from 21:00Z through 03:00Z as the overnight range compressed. The European morning lifted risk twice, at 05:00Z and 08:00Z, both recorded as trend-down. Through the Tuesday U.S. session Tail rebuilt from 18 at 11:00Z to a 24 peak at 15:00Z as the index worked lower and the 10-year pushed above 5%, then eased steadily to 22 at 16:00Z and 21 at 17:00Z once the session low began to hold. No hour after 08:00Z reached the block band. Dominant mode was recorded as mixed in 21 of the 24 hours, consistent with severe macro stress combined with a two-sided intraday price path.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail holds at 20 for the current hour, ticks to 21 for the 19:00Z power hour that carries the danger window, then steps back to 20 into the 20:00Z cash close. It drops below the watch band from 21:00Z and reaches the horizon low of 15 across the Asian hours, where the published lookback shows the calmest conditions of the cycle. From the European pre-market it rebuilds stepwise, re-entering the watch band at 07:00Z and reaching 21 by 08:00Z on Wednesday. It tops the horizon at 24 for the 13:00Z slot that contains the U.S. cash open, one hour after the scheduled retail sales release, before easing to 22 across the afternoon and finishing at 23 for the final hour before the FOMC decision. No hour in this horizon is forecast into the block band, because future structure is conditional and none of it is yet observed. The FOMC decision at 18:00Z Wednesday falls just beyond this horizon.
